items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: and we were all in this town at the same time, and so we had a jam session at this girls' house

ctx.x: Now, Sir Charles, what did Buck mean to you, where did you meet him, and what came off that meeting?

I met Buck Clayton in Parsons, Kansas at a house right down the street from where we lived. And there was a girl there who had a piano and she was not a good pianist but she was interested in music, and several of the guys in the neighborhood, including myself, were interested in her. And in that town Buck Clayton had come home to visit his parents. His father was a minister in that town, and there was another famous musician whose name was Bill Davis, the organist. His father was a minister there, and we were…

Kansas, which was just across the river from Kansas City, Missouri. And I had met Charlie Parker at that time who became famous later. And I had heard a lot of these jazz musicians and I got this sound in my ear, you know. I didn't go in the night clubs but I had heard these musicians at jam sessions. And that's when Charlie Parker started out.
